formation.title: The Oyo Empire Rises
formation.text:
The scattered Yoruba kingdoms have been united under a single Alaafin. From the sacred city of Ile-Ife to the frontier marches, the Oyo Empire now commands the allegiance of millions. But what kind of empire shall this be? The memory of Sango (the third Alaafin, deified as the god of thunder) calls for military glory and cavalry supremacy. Yet the Oyo Mesi, the council of seven, reminds us that Oyo's true strength lies not in the charge of horsemen alone but in the constitutional balance that prevents any single hand from holding too much power. The Bashorun awaits our answer. The Ogboni elders watch. The decision we make now will echo through the ages.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Let the thunder speak! Sango rides with our cavalry.

modifiers.name: Thunder of Sango
modifiers.text: The deified Alaafin Sango, lord of thunder and lightning, watches over our horsemen. In his name, the cavalry charges that shook the savanna shall echo once more.

options.text: The Oyo Mesi shall guide us. No king rules alone.

modifiers.name: Voice of the Oyo Mesi
modifiers.text: The seven councilors speak for the people. Through the wisdom of the Bashorun and the balance of the Ogboni, no tyrant shall reign unchecked in Oyo.

advances.name: Ile-Ife Sacred Origins
advances.text: The spiritual legacy of Ile-Ife, cradle of the Yoruba people, infuses our empire with divine purpose and cultural depth.

advances.name: Mounted Traditions
advances.text: Contact with the Nupe and Saharan peoples taught the Yoruba the art of mounted warfare, beginning a cavalry tradition that would define Oyo's military identity.

advances.name: Ogboni Authority
advances.text: The Ogboni secret society, composed of elder freemen, serves as a judicial check on both the Alaafin and the Oyo Mesi.

advances.name: Yoruba Craft Guilds
advances.text: Specialized artisan guilds produce cloth, ironwork, beads, and pottery of remarkable quality for both local use and export.

advances.name: Walled Towns
advances.text: Massive earthen fortifications, the odi, surround Yoruba towns, providing formidable defense against raiders and rival kingdoms.

advances.name: Yam Cultivation
advances.text: Intensive farming of yams and grains sustains the dense populations of Yoruba towns and cities.

advances.name: Oyo Mesi Council
advances.text: The seven principal councilors of the empire serve as both electoral college and legislative body, representing the voice of the nation.

advances.name: Eso Cavalry Training
advances.text: At the barracks of Ikoyi, the seventy Eso war chiefs train the empire's elite cavalry in the art of mounted combat.

event.title: The Eso of Ikoyi
event.text: At the barracks of Ikoyi, seventy junior war chiefs have been formally invested as the Eso: the empire's elite cavalry corps. Nominated by the Oyo Mesi and confirmed by the Alaafin, these warriors live by a code comparable to the chivalric orders of distant lands. The Eso will form the backbone of our armies, but a question arises: should they remain a distinct elite corps answerable only to the Alaafin, or should they be distributed among the provincial armies to strengthen the whole?

options.text: The Eso are the Alaafin's own: a sword apart.

modifiers.name: Spirit of the Eso
modifiers.text: The seventy war chiefs of Ikoyi ride as one, an elite cavalry corps whose dedication inspires awe.

options.text: Spread them wide. Every army shall benefit from their skill.

modifiers.name: Cavalry Integration
modifiers.text: The Eso's expertise has been distributed throughout the army, raising the quality of every formation.

advances.name: Afin Palace Tradition
advances.text: The Afin, the Alaafin's palace complex, serves as the ceremonial and administrative heart of the Oyo Empire.

advances.name: Sango Cult
advances.text: The worship of Sango, the deified third Alaafin and lord of thunder, reinforces royal legitimacy and inspires devotion.

advances.name: Trans-Saharan Horse Trade
advances.text: Oyo's cavalry depends on a steady supply of horses imported across the Sahara, exchanged for kola nuts, textiles, and other goods.

advances.name: Textile Industry
advances.text: Yoruba weavers produce the celebrated aso-oke cloth, a luxury textile traded across West Africa and beyond.

advances.name: Bashorun Institution
advances.text: The Bashorun, head of the Oyo Mesi, serves as prime minister with the authority to check even the Alaafin himself.

event.title: The Bashorun Ascendant
event.text: The Bashorun, head of the Oyo Mesi, has grown in authority. As prime minister of the empire, the Bashorun now commands influence that rivals the Alaafin himself. In the most extreme cases, tradition grants the Bashorun the terrible power of the calabash: the right to present the Alaafin with parrot eggs, compelling ritual abdication if his reign has descended into tyranny. This is the constitutional genius of Oyo: power checked by power, authority balanced by accountability. But which way shall the balance tip?

options.text: The Bashorun speaks for the people. Strengthen the council.

modifiers.name: Bashorun Ascendancy
modifiers.text: The Bashorun and Oyo Mesi exercise strong oversight, ensuring accountable governance at the cost of decisive royal action.

options.text: The Alaafin is sovereign. Reassert royal authority.

modifiers.name: Alaafin Resurgent
modifiers.text: The Alaafin has reasserted the divine mandate of the throne, concentrating authority for swift and decisive rule.

advances.name: Tributary System
advances.text: Through military pressure and diplomatic craft, Oyo has established a network of tributary states, including the powerful Kingdom of Dahomey.

event.title: Dahomey Subjugated
event.text: After years of campaign, the Kingdom of Dahomey has been forced to accept Oyo suzerainty. Annual tribute in cowrie shells, cloth, and slaves shall flow northward to the Alaafin's court. More importantly, Oyo now controls the routes to the coastal ports (Ajase, Badagry, and the lagoon towns) opening the empire to Atlantic commerce. The Fon kings may chafe under our yoke, but for now the cavalry of the Eso has spoken, and Dahomey has listened.

options.text: Let the tribute flow. Oyo's reach extends to the sea.

advances.name: Royal Market Networks
advances.text: The Oja Oba, royal markets regulated under the Alaafin's authority, serve as the empire's commercial arteries.

advances.name: Ifa Divination
advances.text: The Ifa oracle, administered by the priests of Orunmila, preserves a vast corpus of sacred verses encoding Yoruba knowledge and wisdom.

advances.name: Ajase Atlantic Trade
advances.text: Through the coastal port of Ajase, Oyo connects to the Atlantic trading world, exchanging goods with European and American merchants.

advances.name: Egungun Tradition
advances.text: The Egungun masquerade cult honors departed ancestors, reinforcing social bonds and cultural identity across the empire.

advances.name: Aare-Ona-Kakanfo
advances.text: The supreme military commander, required to live on the frontier, embodies Oyo's ingenious solution to the problem of military power threatening political stability.

event.title: The Aare-Ona-Kakanfo
event.text: A new institution has been established: the Aare-Ona-Kakanfo, supreme commander of all Oyo's armies in the field. By tradition, the Aare-Ona-Kakanfo must reside in a frontier province, keeping the empire's greatest warrior far from the capital and any temptation to seize the throne. He personally commands every campaign, and his authority on the battlefield is absolute. This is Oyo's answer to the eternal dilemma of military states: how to maintain a powerful army without letting its commander become a threat to the state.

options.text: The frontier shall never be unguarded.

advances.name: Horse Archers of the Provinces
advances.text: The provincial towns send light horse trained in archery to the wars of the seventeenth century. They extend the empire's reach across the savanna, screening the Esho and the heavy cavalry and raiding enemy supply lines.

advances.name: Vassal Administration
advances.text: Oyo's sophisticated tributary system extracts wealth and loyalty from subject kingdoms while allowing them significant autonomy.

advances.name: Kola Nut Dominance
advances.text: Control over the kola nut trade, the stimulant prized across the Sahel and beyond, gives Oyo enormous economic leverage.

advances.name: Constitutional Balance
advances.text: The tripartite balance of Alaafin, Oyo Mesi, and Ogboni ensures that no single institution can dominate Oyo's governance.

advances.name: Ogun Metalworking
advances.text: Under the patronage of Ogun, deity of iron and war, Yoruba smiths forge weapons and tools of exceptional quality.

advances.name: Yoruba Urbanization
advances.text: The dense, prosperous cities of Yorubaland are among the largest in West Africa, centers of craft, trade, and cultural life.

advances.name: Indigo Dyeing Trade
advances.text: Yoruba dyers master the art of indigo, producing richly colored textiles that command premium prices in regional markets.

advances.name: Balogun System
advances.text: Provincial war chiefs, the Balogun, command professional armies, providing a disciplined military hierarchy beneath the Aare-Ona-Kakanfo.

advances.name: Diplomatic Craft
advances.text: Oyo's diplomats navigate complex relationships with European traders, neighboring kingdoms, and tributary states with sophistication.

advances.name: Agricultural Reform
advances.text: Improved farming techniques and land management sustain the empire's growing population and urban centers.

advances.name: Firearms Adoption
advances.text: European firearms are integrated into Oyo's military alongside the traditional cavalry, creating a versatile combined-arms force.

advances.name: Atlantic Commerce
advances.text: The port of Ajase flourishes as Oyo's gateway to the Atlantic world, channeling wealth from intercontinental trade.

advances.name: Royal Jurisprudence
advances.text: The codification of Yoruba customary law strengthens the empire's legal framework and extends royal authority.

advances.name: Political Resilience
advances.text: Oyo's constitutional traditions prove their worth in times of crisis, enabling the empire to survive internal upheaval.

advances.name: Military Adaptation
advances.text: The empire adapts its military traditions to the changing nature of warfare, blending cavalry prowess with modern tactics.

advances.name: Yoruba Cultural Renaissance
advances.text: A flowering of Yoruba arts, literature, and philosophy reinforces cultural identity in an era of global transformation.

advances.name: Market Modernization
advances.text: Traditional Yoruba markets evolve into sophisticated commercial centers, integrating new goods and trading methods.

advances.name: Confederal Reform
advances.text: Decentralized governance allows diverse peoples to maintain their identities while contributing to the empire's strength.

advances.name: Diaspora Traditions
advances.text: Yoruba cultural influence spreads far beyond the empire's borders, carried by traders, scholars, and the currents of history.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Oyo Empire
destiny.text: The Oyo Empire has been proclaimed. A stable foundation must be laid before the empire can pursue its greater ambitions.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Oyo Destiny
event.text: The Alaafin sits upon the throne of a stable empire. From the sacred groves of Ile-Ife to the frontier towns, the Oyo people look to their sovereign with expectation. What began as a union of Yoruba kingdoms now stands ready to become something greater. The question is not whether Oyo shall rise, but how high.

options.text: The destiny of Oyo is written in the stars.

destiny.name: Subjugation of Nupe
destiny.text: The Nupe kingdom has long rivaled Oyo for control of the Middle Niger. Conquer Bida and Lokoja to secure the empire's northern flank and open the road to the Sahel. The Eso must first have their seat: raise Ikoyi into a town, or build them an Ile Ikoyi.

conditions.text: Chose Thunder of Sango
Own Bida, or a subject owns it
Own Lokoja, or a subject owns it
We own Ikoyi and it is a town or larger, or one of our locations has an Ile Ikoyi

event.title: The Nupe Subjugated
event.text: The cavalry of the Eso have thundered across the Niger and broken the power of the Nupe kingdom. Bida, their ancient capital, now flies the banner of the Alaafin. The Middle Niger, long contested, is ours. Control of Lokoja at the confluence of the Niger and Benue rivers gives us command of the great waterways. The road to the Sahel lies open.

options.text: The Nupe shall learn to serve the Alaafin.

destiny.name: The Hausa Campaign
destiny.text: With Nupe broken, the wealthy Hausa city-states of Kano and Katsina beckon. Their markets, dye pits, and leather works represent the richest prizes in the western Sudan.

conditions.text: Own Kano, or a subject owns it
Own Katsina, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Fall of Kano
event.text: The great walls of Kano have fallen to Oyo's cavalry. The Hausa city-states, famed for their wealth, their indigo dye pits, and their role in the trans-Saharan trade, are now subject to the Alaafin's authority. This is a conquest without precedent in Yoruba history. But how shall we govern these distant, wealthy cities? The generals debate: press the advantage with relentless speed, or consolidate our supply lines for the long campaign ahead?

options.text: Strike while the iron is hot. Speed is our weapon.

modifiers.name: Cavalry Supremacy
modifiers.text: The Eso cavalry strikes with devastating speed, overwhelming defenders before they can organize a response.

options.text: Secure our supply lines. The savanna is vast.

modifiers.name: Scorched Savanna
modifiers.text: Oyo's logistical mastery of the savanna ensures our armies are fed while the enemy starves, though the cost of maintaining distant supply lines strains the treasury.

destiny.name: Lord of the Sahel
destiny.text: From the forests of Yorubaland to the sands of the Sahel, the Oyo Empire shall eclipse the old empires of Mali and Songhai. Timbuktu and Gao must acknowledge Sango's thunder, and Oyo-Ile must grow to a development of 18, twice what it was.

conditions.text: Own Timbuktu, or a subject owns it
Own Gao, or a subject owns it
Oyo-Ile is owned and has development of at least 18
Prestige at least 75

event.title: Lord of the Sahel
event.text: From the forests of Yorubaland to the bend of the Niger, from Timbuktu's libraries to Gao's river port, the Oyo Empire now commands a domain that dwarfs the old empires of Mali and Songhai. The Alaafin's name is spoken with awe from the Atlantic coast to the edge of the Sahara. Sango's thunder echoes across the western Sudan. Shall we rule this vast domain through divine authority, or through the pragmatic administration of a settled hegemony?

modifiers.name: Sango's Dominion
modifiers.text: The divine authority of Sango commands swift obedience. Conquered peoples submit to the thunder god's chosen, and new warriors flock to the Alaafin's banner.

options.text: A lasting empire requires lasting institutions.

modifiers.name: Sahel Hegemony
modifiers.text: The vast Sahel has been pacified and integrated into a stable imperial administration, with fortified towns securing the peace.

destiny.name: Coastal Reach
destiny.text: The Oyo Mesi's vision demands control of the coast. Secure Ajase and Accra to establish the empire's maritime commerce and connect Yoruba markets to the Atlantic world.

conditions.text: Chose Voice of the Oyo Mesi
Own Àjàṣẹ́, or a subject owns it
Own Accra, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 1000

event.title: The Ports of the Atlantic
event.text: The Oyo Mesi's strategy bears fruit. Ajase and the coastal towns of the Gold Coast now answer to the Alaafin's merchants. Canoes laden with cloth, kola nuts, and ivory journey down the lagoons to meet European and American traders at the coast. The Yoruba interior, long isolated from the sea, now commands a window onto the Atlantic world. The constitutional architects of the Oyo Mesi have proven that wealth flows more readily to those who trade than to those who merely conquer.

options.text: The sea shall carry Oyo's wealth to the world.

destiny.name: Trade Ascendancy
destiny.text: With coastal ports secured, Yoruba traders must carry our cloth and kola far beyond our borders. Put our merchants to work in three markets, ensure ivory flows through our markets, and dominate the ivory trade.

conditions.text: Num of markets with merchants at least 3
A market the country is in

children.text: Ivory is produced in the market
Ivory is traded in the market

conditions.text: Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Ivory Markets
event.text: Oyo's markets have become the crossroads of West African commerce. Ivory from the interior, cloth from Yoruba looms, kola nuts from the forests, and European goods from the coast all pass through our regulated markets under the watchful eye of the Oyo Mesi. Our merchants keep their stalls in three markets, and the empire's commercial reach rivals that of distant trading powers. But how shall we deploy this commercial might? Shall we build grand market cities, or invest in the roads and relationships that sustain trade?

options.text: Build the markets. Let traders come to us.

modifiers.name: Market Mastery
modifiers.text: Oyo's regulated markets have become the commercial engine of West Africa, though the expanding bureaucracy demands its share.

options.text: Invest in the roads. Trade follows the path.

modifiers.name: Ivory Roads
modifiers.text: Trade routes radiating from Oyo carry ivory, cloth, and kola nuts to distant markets, binding diverse peoples into a shared commercial culture.

destiny.name: The Merchant Empire
destiny.text: The constitutional genius of the Oyo Mesi has built an empire of commerce. Extend our trade networks to Kumasi and Djenne, the great market cities of West Africa, and keep a Royal Market in four locations.

conditions.text: Own Kumasi, or a subject owns it
Own Djenné, or a subject owns it
At least 4 owned locations have an Oja Oba
Prestige at least 75

event.title: The Merchant Empire
event.text: From Kumasi in the west to Djenne on the Niger, Oyo's merchants dominate the trade of West Africa. The Oyo Mesi's constitutional vision has created something unprecedented: an empire built not on cavalry charges but on contract law, regulated markets, and diplomatic finesse. The Alaafin reigns but does not rule alone; the council governs but cannot overreach. This balance, refined over generations, has produced an empire of remarkable stability and prosperity. What shall be its ultimate expression?

options.text: The council's wisdom is the empire's strength.

modifiers.name: Oyo Mesi Ascendant
modifiers.text: The constitutional mastery of the Oyo Mesi has produced an empire of laws, roads, and diplomatic sophistication unmatched in West Africa.

options.text: Open the gates. Oyo trades with all the world.

modifiers.name: Atlantic Gateway
modifiers.text: Oyo's coastal ports connect the interior to the Atlantic world, channeling wealth from intercontinental commerce into the empire's heartland.

units.name: Ilari Royal Guard
units.text: The Ilari are the Alaafin's personal bodyguard, identifiable by their half-shaved heads. Drawn from the palace household, they serve as both guards and messengers of royal authority.

units.name: Oyo Heavy Cavalry
units.text: Armored horsemen mounted on large horses imported from across the Sahara. These heavy cavalry deliver devastating shock charges that shatter enemy formations.

units.name: Oyo Heavy Cavalry
units.text: Noble cavalrymen raised through the levy system, fighting in the heavy cavalry tradition of the Oyo Empire.

units.name: Balogun Guard
units.text: Professional infantry serving under provincial war chiefs. The Balogun Guard represents the evolution of Oyo's military from cavalry dominance to combined-arms warfare.

units.name: Savanna Horse Archers
units.text: Light horse of the provincial towns, armed with bows and javelins. Where the titled Esho charge home, these riders scout, turn a flank and harass across the open savanna, on mounts bought from the north.

buildings.name: Afin
buildings.text: The Alaafin's palace complex, a sprawling compound of courtyards, audience halls, and ritual spaces that serves as the political and ceremonial heart of the empire.

buildings.name: Oja Oba
buildings.text: A royal market regulated under the Alaafin's authority, where merchants from across West Africa trade in kola nuts, textiles, livestock, and luxury goods.

buildings.name: Ogboni Lodge
buildings.text: The meeting place of the Ogboni secret society, where elder freemen deliberate on matters of justice, religion, and the proper limits of royal power.

buildings.name: Ile Ikoyi
buildings.text: The barracks and training grounds of the Eso cavalry corps at Ikoyi, where the seventy junior war chiefs hone their skills in mounted combat.

buildings.name: Sango Shrine
buildings.text: A temple dedicated to Sango, the deified Alaafin and lord of thunder, where devotees honor the deity with bata drums and ritual offerings.

buildings.name: Ile Ise
buildings.text: A house of Yoruba weavers and dyers, where cotton is woven on the narrow loom and cloth is steeped in indigo pits in the guild tradition.

buildings.name: Kola Grove
buildings.text: A planted grove of kola trees in the forest country, owned and tended tree by tree. The nuts are chewed, offered to guests and gods, and carried north across the savanna, where they are paid for in horses. The grove raises what the land yields, and it can stand only where the land yields medicinal plants.

where.text: The location's raw material is Medicaments

buildings.name: Odi
buildings.text: A massive earthen fortification wall surrounding a Yoruba town, built from packed earth and reinforced with timber. These walls could reach heights of twenty feet.

buildings.name: Ile Bata
buildings.text: A drum house where master drummers craft and play the sacred bata drums, used in Sango worship and as a long-distance communication system across the empire.

buildings.name: Oko Oba
buildings.text: A royal farmstead for organized yam cultivation. Yams were the dietary foundation of Oyo's population and the agricultural surplus that sustained its imperial ambitions. Worked in order for the palace, the farm raises more from the land around it than the scattered plots of the villages.

where.text: The location's raw material is Sturdy Grains

buildings.name: Igbodu
buildings.text: The grove of Ifa at the edge of the town. Here the babalawo are initiated, and spend years learning by heart the verses of the two hundred and fifty-six odu.

buildings.name: Agbede
buildings.text: The forge of a Yoruba town. A shrine to Ogun stands by the anvil, and no smith begins work before the deity has been greeted.

buildings.name: Ile Ogun
buildings.text: A sacred war shrine dedicated to Ogun, deity of iron and warfare, serving as both arsenal and spiritual center for the empire's military campaigns.

buildings.name: Ile Owu
buildings.text: A grand merchant guild house where Yoruba traders, governed by the Oyo Mesi's commercial regulations, coordinate the empire's far-reaching trade networks.

list.name: Oyo Mesi
list.text: The seven hereditary chiefs of metropolitan Oyo (the Bashorun, Agbaakin, Samu, Alapini, Laguna, Akiniku, and Asipa) whose offices ran in seven specific clans of the capital. They ratified each Alaafin's accession, audited the treasury, and held the constitutional right to present a king with the calabash of parrot's eggs that ordered him to commit suicide. The Bashorun Gaha exercised this prerogative serially from the 1750s until Alaafin Abiodun overthrew him in 1774.

list.name: Ogboni Society
list.text: The secret initiatory brotherhood of senior men sworn to the earth-deity Onile, distinguished by the paired bronze edan figurines worn around the neck. The iledi lodge functioned as the town's court of last instance for capital cases and pronounced the metaphysical verdict required before any Yoruba king could be deposed. Ogboni magistrates effectively ran Egba Abeokuta after 1830, and parallel Osugbo lodges governed Ijebu well into the colonial era.

conditions.text: Isese religion

list.name: Eso and Aare-Ona-Kakanfo
list.text: The seventy titled cavalry officers of the Eso, personally appointed by the Alaafin, served under the Aare-Ona-Kakanfo, the supreme field-general constitutionally forbidden to quarter inside the capital. The Kakanfo was bound by oath to win battles or commit suicide, and his provincial seat (at Ikoyi, then Iwoye, finally Ilorin) was meant to prevent military coups. In 1817 Aare Afonja inverted the design when he revolted from Ilorin and broke Old Oyo.

list.name: Ilari Title-Bearers
list.text: Several hundred royal officials (some male, some female, all distinguished by a head shaved on one side and dyed with indigo or camwood on the other) drawn from royal slaves, captives, and clients rather than from the metropolitan free clans. They served as the Alaafin's messengers, tribute-collectors, resident envoys, and executors of royal warrants. Because their offices were personal and revocable, the Ilari corps was the throne's bureaucratic counterweight to the lineage-based power of the Oyo Mesi.

list.name: Ajele Provincial Residency
list.text: The senior Ilari posted as permanent residents at the courts of the empire's tributary kings, of Egba, Egbado, Onko, Ijebu, Ketu, Owu, and most importantly the Fon kingdom of Dahomey, which paid annual tribute to Oyo from c.1730 to 1818. The Ajele assessed tribute, audited the local king's accounts, and forwarded annual remittances of slaves, cowries, cloth, and ivory to Oyo-Ile. Their extortions were a major driver of the 1817-1836 rebellions that ended the empire.

list.name: Babalawo Ifa Council
list.text: The college of senior babalawo ('fathers of secrets') who consulted Ifa divination on every major royal decision: the choice of a new Alaafin from among the eligible princes, the timing of wars, the propitiation required to lift a famine, the signs against a tributary's loyalty. Reading the cast of sixteen palm-nuts against a corpus of 256 Odu verses, the Awo's authority crossed every Yoruba kingdom and was respected by the Fon (as Fa) and the Edo. Their annual consultation at Ile-Ife bound the empire's religious life to a single divinatory tradition.

conditions.text: Isese religion
